profile.summary: OpenFold3 is an open reproduction of AlphaFold 3 by the AlQuraishi Lab at Columbia University and the OpenFold consortium. It predicts the structure of a biomolecular complex from its sequences, covering standard and non-canonical protein, RNA and DNA chains together with small molecules, and it writes coordinates in mmCIF with per-sample confidence files. Unlike most reproductions it also ships the training code and the training datasets, including a 13 million sequence distillation set, so the model can be retrained from scratch. The published versions are research previews: the model is called OpenFold3-preview and the developers say the final model is still in development.

summary_quotes.text:
OpenFold3-preview is a biomolecular structure prediction model aiming to be a bitwise reproduction of DeepMind's 
[AlphaFold3](https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphafold3), developed by the AlQuraishi Lab at Columbia University and the OpenFold consortium.
Structure prediction of standard and non-canonical protein, RNA, and DNA chains, and small molecules

making OF3p2 the only
functionally reproducible AF3 reproduction that is trainable from scratch and near AF3 parity
The final OpenFold3 model is still in development

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model follows the AlphaFold 3 design and input features, which the developers set out to reproduce bitwise. Alignments are built either from the ColabFold server or with JackHMMER and hhblits following the AlphaFold 3 protocol, and templates can be supplied for protein monomers. Training follows the AlphaFold 3 supplementary information. For OpenFold3-preview2 that meant 155,000 steps in total, split into 131,500 steps of initial training, 8,000 steps of fine-tuning stage 1 and 15,500 steps of fine-tuning stage 2, on 256 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Unlike AlphaFold 3 the team skipped the third fine-tuning stage and trained the PAE confidence head from the start. Inference can use kernel acceleration through cuEquivariance and DeepSpeed4Science, spread one job across several GPUs, and run in a low memory mode.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three parameter sets are documented, each tied to a range of software releases. The current default is openbind-2025-06-30-174k, file of3-ob-2025-06-30-174k.pt, at 174,000 training steps, trained with what the README calls the forthcoming OpenFold3 architecture and a June 2025 training cutoff. The two earlier sets are marked deprecated: openfold3-p2-155k, file of3-p2-155k.pt, at 155,000 steps, and openfold3-p1, file of3_ft3_v1.pt, at 78,000 steps. Older parameters need an older release, for example pip install openfold3 < 0.5 for the preview2 weights, and setup_openfold must be rerun after changing version. A result must therefore name both the parameter set and the package version. The repository cites itself as version 0.4.2 with DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19001000, and the packaging file carries a fallback version of 0.5.1.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: All-atom biomolecular structure prediction model, an open reproduction of AlphaFold 3, released as a research preview.

quotes.text: aiming to be a bitwise reproduction of DeepMind's
This research preview is intended to gather community feedback and allow developers to start building on top of the OpenFold ecosystem.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: The AlphaFold 3 architecture, reproduced: the same input features, and training following the AlphaFold 3 supplementary information. The default OpenBind-0 parameters were trained with what the README calls the forthcoming OpenFold3 architecture, which the sources read do not describe further.

quotes.text: OpenFold3-preview replicates the input features described in the [AlphaFold3](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07487-w) publication
We followed the hyperparameter configuration of the AF3 SI

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A query JSON naming the chains and ligands of the complex, with alignments either generated through the ColabFold MSA server or precomputed, and optional structure templates for protein monomers. Several queries can be given in one job.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Predicted structures as mmCIF files, one per diffusion sample and seed, with per-sample confidence JSON files and an aggregated confidence file, as the example outputs in the weights repository show.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The Protein Data Bank plus the team's own distillation sets, all released. The monomer distillation set follows the AlphaFold 3 recipe on the clustered 2025_03 release of MGnify: alignments for about 5 million sequences through JackHMMER on UniRef90, UniProt and MGnify with an updated BFD through HHblits, plus 10 million more through the ColabFold MMseqs2 protocol, filtered at Neff above 4.0 to keep 8 of those 10 million, with structures predicted by OpenFold and the more confident of two predictions kept. The RNA distillation set follows the AlphaFold 3 protocol on RFAM v15.1 and retains about 125,000 predicted structures after filtering at average PDE below 2.
facts.source_locator: technical report: Dataset Updates; README: Datasets

quotes.text:
We used the clustered 2025_03 release of the Mgnify [2]
database, selecting cluster representatives from clusters with three or more members.

For
approximately 5M sequences, we generated MSAs using the standard OF3 MSA pipeline which
searches UniRef90, UniProt, and Mgnify sequence databases with JackHMMer [14] and an
updated BFD database with HHblits [15].

we removed sequences with an Neff <= 4.0, keeping 8M/10M sequences
after this step

Instead
of RFAM v14.9 we used the current RFAM (v15.1) [5]

After filtering for structures with an average PDE<2, approximately 125,000 predicted
RNA structures remained.
We provide the full training data for reproducing OpenFold3-preview, including our reproduction of the MGnify-based 13M-sequence distillation dataset described in the AlphaFold3 paper.

quotes.text:
This second prerelease includes updated model weights, updated inference and
training code, and all datasets needed for training and assessment
[Training data processing](https://openfold-3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data_pipeline_reference.html) and [model training](https://openfold-3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/training.html)

strengths.text: The engineering for large or awkward jobs is in place: kernel acceleration, multi-query batches, predictions distributed over several GPUs, and a low memory mode for small cards.

quotes.text: Custom settings for [memory constrained GPU resources](https://openfold-3.readthedocs.io/en/latest/inference.html#inference-low-memory-mode)

strengths.text: The developers document their own bugs and errata, including a template mask fault, a missing template filter, a plDDT computation fault and a distillation set generated with a backend that reduced chemical validity.

quotes.text: We identified multiple model and data-related bugs in our previous version, OF3p.

The version of the RNA distillation set used during training OF3p2 was generated using the
rocBLASLt backend on MI300A APUs, which we retrospectively found to result in structures with
decreased chemical validity.

run_guide.summary: Install the package, let the setup command download the default parameters, and predict the bundled ubiquitin example using the ColabFold alignment server.
prerequisites: A Hugging Face account that has accepted the OpenFold3 gate, since the OpenFold3-preview weights there are gated with an automatic form.
A GPU: the documentation offers kernel acceleration, multi-GPU distribution and a low memory mode, and no CPU-only route is described in the sources read.
Network access to the ColabFold MSA server for the quick start, or precomputed alignments instead.
Apache-2.0 terms for the code and the OpenFold3-preview weights; the licence of the default OpenBind-0 weights is not stated in the sources read.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and the documentation and have not been executed by Rewire.

The example query path assumes the repository's examples folder, which the pip package may not place in the working directory; the documentation and the Hugging Face examples folder hold further input files.
The quick start sends sequences to the public ColabFold MSA server. Use the precomputed alignment route for anything confidential.

notes: Two of the developers' own sources disagree on the default parameter set: the README says the default shipped with OpenFold3 0.5.0 and later is OpenBind-0, and the parameters table marks openbind-2025-06-30-174k as the default, while the resolution flowchart on the same documentation page still says 'Use default model: openfold3-p2-155k'. Treat the flowchart as stale, and name the parameter set explicitly in any run. The record's description is phrased in interface-confidence terms from the POISK benchmark (existing source poisk-20261115-source-manuscript-v1); OpenFold3 is a general structure predictor. The repository name is openfold-3 and the model is OpenFold3-preview; the final OpenFold3 is not released. The technical report covers preview2, not the current OpenBind-0 default, whose announcement post was not fetched. Both the documentation page and the technical report are stored here as extracted text rather than the original HTML and PDF bytes. The default OpenBind-0 file of3-ob-2025-06-30-174k.pt is not listed in the OpenFold/OpenFold3 Hugging Face repository at the revision read, and no saved file states where it is hosted or under what licence, so its weights_url, gated and weights_licence are null.
